newsitem.title: USA: Rifkind says Mideast peace could be near collapse.
newsitem.headline: Rifkind says Mideast peace could be near collapse.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Thursday the Middle East peace process could be on the verge of collapse following bloody clashes between Israelis and Palestinians on the West Bank.

Rifkind was speaking before talks with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, who said he had no plans at present to visit the Middle East, although Washington was willing to do what it could to ease the crisis.

"It would be difficult to exaggerate the gravity of the situation," Rifkind said. He said the clashes were the symptom of "a very deep deterioration in the peace process, with a very real danger that the peace process could be on the verge of collapse".

Christopher said that although it was a "serious situation", the peace process had "proved quite durable" in the past and had survived a series of guerrilla bombings in Israel last February and March.

Asked if the crisis demanded that he return to the region, Christopher told reporters: "I don't have any plans to do so but ... we're prepared to do whatever would be helpful to the parties in the situation."
Christopher and Rifkind were in New York to attend the current United Nations General Assembly session.
